summary.text: The decolonisation of Africa was a series of political developments from the mid-1950s to 1976, during the Cold War, as colonial governments gave way to sovereign states.
Colonial rule came from the Scramble for Africa, when European powers claimed almost all of the continent between 1870 and 1914, and its end often involved violence and organised revolts.
By 1977, 50 African countries had gained independence from European colonial powers.

facts.label: Time span
facts.value: Mid-1950s to 1976, during the Cold War

facts.label: Kept sovereignty
facts.value: Liberia and the Ethiopian Empire were the exceptions

facts.label: Africans in European armies
facts.value: Approximately one million sub-Saharan Africans in World War II

items.prompt: European powers confirmed the partition of Africa at a conference in 1885, ignoring existing political and social structures. What happened to Africa's precolonial states?

options.label: Most kept their sovereignty under European protection
Almost all lost their sovereignty, with Liberia and Ethiopia the exceptions
Most merged into one African federation
Most became allies of the colonisers on equal terms

items.explain: Almost all precolonial states lost their sovereignty; only Liberia and the Ethiopian Empire were exceptions.

items.prompt: An African soldier returns home after serving a colonial power in World War II. What was a likely result of that service?

options.label: Deeper political awareness and expectations of more self-determination
A guarantee of equal treatment from the colonial regime
Public praise from colonial powers for his contribution
A prompt withdrawal of colonial powers from his homeland

items.explain: Service led to deeper political awareness and expectations of respect and self-determination, which went largely unfulfilled; colonial powers downplayed Africans' contributions.

items.prompt: Roosevelt and Churchill issued a charter about people choosing their own government. Churchill said it covered only nations of Europe under Nazi rule, while Roosevelt thought it applied worldwide. How did anticolonial politicians read it?

options.label: As covering only the nations of Europe
As a binding treaty approved by both legislatures
As having no bearing on their own situation
As relevant to colonial empires right away

items.explain: Anticolonial politicians immediately saw the Atlantic Charter as relevant to colonial empires, even though it was not a ratified treaty.

items.prompt: A mining company in a colony sends its profits to shareholders in Europe while local development is neglected. What did this cause?

options.label: Rapid growth of local industry paid for by those profits
Wider local support for colonial government
Significant local socioeconomic grievances
Calls for more European shareholders to invest

items.explain: Diverting profits to European shareholders at the expense of internal development caused significant local socioeconomic grievances.

items.prompt: In the 1930s, colonial powers helped educate a small elite of local African leaders at Western universities. What did those leaders become familiar with there?

options.label: Ideas such as self-determination
Methods for keeping colonial rule permanent
The plans for dividing Africa among European powers
Orders to enlist in European armies

items.explain: At Western universities these leaders became familiar with ideas such as self-determination.

items.prompt: A 1960 international declaration said colonial exploitation denies human rights. What did it say should happen to power?

options.label: It should stay with colonial powers until they chose to leave
It should be transferred back to the countries or territories concerned
It should pass to the United Nations to run directly
It should be shared equally with the colonial powers

items.explain: The UN declaration stated that power should be transferred back to the countries or territories concerned.
